editorial:
Ever wonder how one man could trick the entire world out of billions of dollars? You get a front-row seat to that disaster here. You will follow Bernie Madoff, a guy who looked like a successful businessman but was actually running the biggest lie in history. The vibe is heavy and tense because you see him juggling his fake accounts while his family has no clue what is going on. It feels like watching a slow-motion car crash where you know everything is about to blow up, but you cannot look away from the greed and the lies.

Robert De Niro does an amazing job playing Madoff; he makes the character feel cold and calculating. The pacing is steady, though it focuses more on the talking and the stress than big action scenes. If you love true crime stories that show the dark side of money, you will really dig this. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you want something that makes you think about trust.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Madoff finally tells his sons the truth about his fake business. He tries to push them to help him end his life, but they turn him in to the police instead. You see him get arrested and sent to prison for a very long time. The movie wraps up by showing the sad reality of the victims who lost their life savings and a family that was completely torn apart by one man's lies.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves real-life crime stories and financial scandals.
